newsitem.title: ABU DHABI: SOCCER-LEBANON TO HOST ASIAN CUP IN 2000.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-LEBANON TO HOST ASIAN CUP IN 2000.

text.p: Lebanon will host the 12th Asian Cup in the year 2000, the Asian Football Confederation (AFC) announced on Saturday.
Fourteen members of the AFC's 16-member executive committee voted for Lebanon. Two voted for China.
Malaysia, Hong Kong and South Korea had all withdrawn their bids in the run-up to the vote.
The choice of Lebanon breaches a 40-year-old unwritten agreement that the competition should alternate every four years between east and west Asia.
Lebanese soccer officials, clearly delighted by the vote, said they hoped the choice would give the game a great boost in Lebanon and help speed up the country's reconstruction.
Lebanon is still recovering from the 1975-90 civil war. Prime Minister Rafik al-Hariri's government has launched a multi-billion dollar plan to rebuild the country.
''We hope that this decision will help speed up the process of rebuilding Lebanon,'' said Rahif Alameh, head of Lebanon's soccer federation and a member of the AFC executive committee.
''Our work has just started. We now will embark on a campaign to build and rehabilitate our stadiums and begin preparations to make the competition one of the best ever,'' he told reporters.

Lebanon has already located $55 million to rehabilitate three main soccer stadiums and a few training grounds. The construction of an Arab-financed sports city in Beirut is underway -- though well behind schedule.
The 2000 Cup will be played in five stadiums, with 20 training grounds available for the teams, Lebanese officials said.
It will involve 16 teams for the first time.
